A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dynamic Reflections with the same authors and empirical framework. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including v2's new theoretical Appendix B.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-text alignment measurements, frame/caption scaling experiments, and temporal-order sensitivity analyses, with additional empirical results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses in the main text and Appendix A, alongside the added theoretical discussion.

M1.justification: The mutual k-NN framework, layer selection, frame/subclip aggregation, caption concatenation, and fitted scaling-law form remain unchanged. Appendix B supplies theoretical models explaining the existing procedure, without introducing an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain VaTeX and PVD alignment, Kinetics-400 and SSv2 retrieval, the same downstream perception tasks, and Test of Time and VideoComp temporal evaluation. No dataset or distinct task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The model inventory in Appendix A.2 and comparator membership in corresponding experiments remain unchanged. Perception Encoder Core Giant remains in Figure 8 despite losing one plotted endpoint; the new theoretical citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated sampling, aggregation, metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged, including 1,024-video alignment sets and 10,000-video retrieval subsets. The omitted Figure 8 endpoint does not establish a revised experimental procedure or rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8 slightly reduces the frame-sensitivity evidence by removing Perception Encoder Core Giant's 64-frame point. Figure 9 also revises the source caption in the caption-synthesis illustration while retaining its frames and synthesized outputs. Other sensitivity, temporal-negative, and cross-model analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same Pearson correlations and p-values. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimation procedures; Appendix B's theoretical noise assumptions are not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 8 removes the pe_core_giant result at 64 frames, so its curve now ends at 48 frames. Other plotted results, alignment heatmaps, and Table 1 match, including VaTeX R-squared values of 0.9791 for VideoMAEv2 Huge and 0.9964 for DINOv2 Giant.

T1.justification: v1 presents the scaling law primarily as an empirical fit. New Appendix B adds two conditional derivations: independent representation noise with manifold approximation yields additive errors and exponents 2/d; a Zipfian feature model uses inclusion-exclusion and a negligible-overlap assumption to recover the law. These introduce substantial mathematical assumptions and reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and main introduction/conclusion retain the same claims about test-time data richness, scaling laws, downstream correlations, and temporal limitations. Appendix B adds support for the existing scaling-law claim without redefining the paper's main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B substantially extends v1's brief coefficient interpretation by linking scaling exponents to effective dimensionality, redundancy, and feature-frequency tails. It also explicitly identifies the MSE proxy, independence assumptions, and neglected cross-modal overlap, and discusses interaction modeling as future work.

D1.justification: Figure 9 replaces the example source text and changes its attribution from a human-provided caption to a fine-grained model caption, clarifying the illustrated input's provenance. The Gemini 2.5 Pro synthesis prompt, model details, and code/data access information remain unchanged; no underlying pipeline change is established.

R1.justification: Beyond v1's brief analogy to Hoffmann et al., Appendix B substantially expands the theoretical grounding through neural scaling laws, manifold approximation, and Zipfian statistics. Added references include Bahri et al., Sharma and Kaplan, Levina and Bickel, and Newman. The original representation-alignment positioning in Section 2 is retained.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives limited edits, the publication header changes, and Section 6 and the appendix overview gain pointers to Appendix B. The main narrative and existing appendix sections remain largely intact; the substantial theoretical addition is not a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The same twelve figures and one table remain. Figure 1 moves earlier, Figure 9's source-caption box and caption are revised, Figure 8 loses one endpoint, and Figures 11–12 move after the new theoretical appendix. The visual design and other displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B improves interpretability by making possible mechanisms and assumptions behind the existing scaling law explicit. Figure 9's revised source also matches details already present in its synthesized captions, improving internal consistency. The gains are limited: the theory depends on an assumed MSE proxy and independence/overlap approximations, while empirical support is essentially unchanged apart from one omitted Figure 8 endpoint.
